texts.li: {A_nameDef} had to put {A_possessive} shoulder to the battered {THING} twice before it gave.
The damaged {THING} stuck again, and {A_nameDef} kicked it open, muttering.
Wrestling the warped {THING} open cost {A_nameDef} a good minute and a skinned knuckle.
The {THING} jammed halfway, and {A_nameDef} had to squeeze through sideways.
{A_nameDef} had to lift the sagging {THING} by its handle to get it to close.
{A_nameDef} shouldered the {THING} open with a load in {A_possessive} arms and nearly dropped the lot.
The {THING} scraped another groove in the floor as {A_nameDef} hauled it open with both hands.
Half off its hinges, the {THING} swung shut on {A_nameDef}'s heel.
Drip, drip, from the hole in the roof. {A_nameDef} spent part of the day moving things out from under it.
{A_nameDef} set a bucket under the leak in the roof, and then a second bucket for the second leak.
[rain] Water dripping through the roof landed on the back of {A_nameDef}'s neck every time {A_pronoun} sat down.
[snow] Snow sifted in through the hole in the roof and settled in a cold drift where {A_nameDef} had to walk.
A puddle was spreading across the floor under the gap in the roof, and {A_nameDef} was the one who stepped in it.
{A_nameDef} moved {A_possessive} bedding twice to get out from under the drip.
[rain] All the time {A_nameDef} worked, water dripped steadily onto the floor beside {A_objective}.
Flies found the {THING} before anyone else did, and {A_nameDef} spent the afternoon swatting them.
{A_nameDef} followed a sour smell to the {THING}, which should have gone somewhere cold days ago.
[summer|hot] The {THING} had started to turn in the heat, and {A_nameDef} could smell it from the doorway.
{A_nameDef} lifted the cloth off the {THING} and put it straight back.
The {THING} has gone soft and gray at the edges, and {A_nameDef} has been telling anyone who'll listen.
{A_nameDef} propped the door open, which did nothing about the {THING}.
There were grubs in the {THING}, and {A_nameDef} wanted it out of the room before supper.
[summer|hot] In this heat the {THING} won't last another day. {A_nameDef} said so at supper, twice.
{A_nameDef} sniffed at the {THING}, then sniffed again to be sure, and wished {A_pronoun} hadn't.
{A_nameDef} banged a shin on the bed frame getting up. There was no room to turn around in there.
{A_nameDef} got dressed with one elbow against the wall, as {A_pronoun} does every morning in that cramped room.
For the third time this week, {A_nameDef} stubbed a toe on the furniture crammed in around {A_possessive} bed.
{A_nameDef} had to move the stool to open the chest, and the chest to open the door.
Pulling on a shirt, {A_nameDef} hit the wall with one elbow and the bed with the other.
{A_nameDef} sat on the bed to pull on {A_possessive} boots, because there was nowhere else to sit.

ColonyCouncil.NuisanceDef.label: a machine droning by the bed

texts.li: The {THING} droned on the other side of the wall all night, and {A_nameDef} heard every minute of it.
{A_nameDef} lay awake listening to the {THING} rattle and hum, and got up tired.
Cloth stuffed in both ears, and {A_nameDef} could still hear the {THING} by the bed.
The hum of the {THING} got into {A_nameDef}'s dreams and stayed there.
{A_nameDef} pulled the blanket over {A_possessive} head against the thump of the {THING}.
Smoke from the {THING} hung under the ceiling, and {A_nameDef}'s eyes were streaming within minutes.
{A_nameDef} came out of the room coughing and smelling of the {THING}.
[cold|winter] {A_nameDef} propped the door open to let the smoke from the {THING} out, and let the cold in instead.
Under the haze from the {THING}, {A_nameDef} worked bent low and coughing.
Soot from the {THING} had settled on everything, and {A_nameDef} came away gray to the elbows.

ColonyCouncil.NuisanceDef.label: a long walk to the table

texts.li: {A_nameDef} made the long walk from bed to breakfast again, and was hungry and short-tempered by the time {A_pronoun} reached the table.
"Takes longer to walk to the table than to eat at it," {A_nameDef} grumbled.
[winter|cold] It was a long, cold walk from {A_nameDef}'s bed to the table, and {A_pronoun} made it with numb feet.
{A_nameDef} counted the steps from bed to table this morning and gave up at three hundred.
The others had finished by the time {A_nameDef} got to the table.
[winter|cold] {A_nameDef} crossed the frozen yard to breakfast with {A_possessive} hands tucked into {A_possessive} armpits.
{A_nameDef} set off from bed to breakfast and stopped twice on the way to rest.
The dining room might as well be in the next valley, according to {A_nameDef}.
{A_nameDef} worked out that {A_pronoun} spends more of the day walking to meals than eating them.
{A_nameDef}'s soup had gone cold by the time {A_pronoun} carried it back across the colony to eat.
[winter|cold] There was frost in {A_nameDef}'s hair by the time {A_pronoun} got to breakfast.
"Has anyone thought of putting a table nearer the beds?" {A_nameDef} asked again.
Mosquitoes found {A_nameDef} the moment {A_pronoun} stepped outside, and followed {A_objective} all the way back in.
Biting flies, all evening. {A_nameDef} has bites on top of bites.
[night] The whine of mosquitoes kept {A_nameDef} swatting at the dark.
{A_nameDef} woke covered in fresh bites and spent breakfast scratching.
A cloud of gnats followed {A_nameDef} across the yard, getting in {A_possessive} eyes and mouth.
There's a ring of bites around each of {A_nameDef}'s ankles from the fields.
[night] {A_nameDef} lay awake while a mosquito found {A_objective} again and again in the dark.
{A_nameDef} slapped {A_possessive} own neck so often today that it went red.
Flies circled {A_nameDef}'s head through the whole of lunch.
{A_nameDef} stepped right in a pile of animal filth and had to scrape {A_possessive} boot on the doorstep.
{A_nameDef} found out where the animals had been the hard way, with {A_possessive} foot.
Two rooms' worth of animal filth went in on {A_nameDef}'s boots before {A_pronoun} noticed.
{A_nameDef} slipped on animal droppings by the door and caught {A_objective}self on the frame.
The day started with {A_nameDef} on {A_possessive} knees, scrubbing animal mess off the floor.
Animal mess on the doorstep again, and {A_nameDef} found it in the dark.
{A_nameDef} cleaned animal muck off {A_possessive} boots with a stick, grumbling.
{A_nameDef} sat down without looking and found out the animals had been there first.
{A_nameDef} picked a way through the things lying everywhere and still couldn't find what {A_pronoun} needed.
{A_nameDef} tripped over a coil of rope that should have been put away days ago.
Half of {A_nameDef}'s shift went on hunting through the mess for the right saw.
{A_nameDef} had to move three piles of junk to reach the workbench.
The hammer was under the sacks, and the sacks were under the planks. {A_nameDef} found it eventually.
{A_nameDef} stepped over the same pile of junk four times before deciding it wasn't {A_possessive} job to move it.
{A_nameDef} put the morning's tools down for a moment and lost them under the heaps.
One careless elbow, and a pile of odds and ends went sliding across the floor. {A_nameDef} spent a while gathering them up.
The seams of {A_nameDef}'s {THING} split again, and {A_pronoun} spent the evening sewing them shut.
{A_nameDef}'s badly made {THING} itched and pinched all day.
{A_nameDef} caught {A_possessive} poorly stitched {THING} on a splinter and tore it again.
{A_nameDef}'s {THING} split along a seam while {A_pronoun} was lifting a crate.
{A_nameDef} picked at a loose thread on {A_possessive} {THING}, and a whole seam came away with it.
{A_nameDef}'s {THING} let the wind straight through at the seams.
{A_nameDef} asked at supper who had made {A_possessive} {THING}, and the room went quiet.
A button came off {A_nameDef}'s {THING} and rolled away under the shelves.
Another night on the {THING}, and {A_nameDef} woke up stiff.
"Real beds," {A_nameDef} said at breakfast, rubbing {A_possessive} back after a night on the {THING}. "I remember those."
[cold|winter] The cold came up through the {THING} all night, and {A_nameDef} got up aching.
{A_nameDef} spent the night trying to find a soft part of the {THING}, and gave up near dawn.
{A_nameDef} got up from the {THING} with the pattern of the floor pressed into {A_possessive} cheek.
A crick in the neck from the {THING}, and all morning {A_nameDef} had to turn {A_possessive} whole body to look at anything.
{A_nameDef} folded {A_possessive} coat into a pillow, which did very little for the {THING}.
{A_nameDef} lay awake on the {THING} feeling every lump in the floor beneath it.
One joint at a time, {A_nameDef} got up from the {THING}.
{A_nameDef} stuffed the {THING} with dry grass, which helped until about midnight.
{A_nameDef} asked over breakfast who in the colony had a real mattress, and looked hard at the answer.
